physics_goals.quote: which was specially designed for precision measurements of single particle spectra and the intensity interferometry in hadronic systems of high energy density using collisions of both hadrons and heavy ions.
physics_goals.value: Precision measurements of single-particle spectra and of particle-pair (Hanbury Brown-Twiss) intensity interferometry in hadronic systems of high energy density, in hadron and heavy-ion collisions

summary.plain: NA44 was a small CERN spectrometer that picked out pions, kaons and protons near mid-rapidity in proton, sulphur and lead collisions. How their momenta and pair correlations changed with system size showed that the fireball expands outward and then freezes out.
summary.technical: NA44: small-acceptance focusing magnetic spectrometer with time-of-flight and a threshold imaging Cherenkov counter (first use of CsI photocathodes) on the H4 beam line of the SPS North Area; single-particle spectra, two-particle interferometry and (anti)deuteron yields in p, S and 158A GeV Pb collisions; evidence for radial flow, thermal freeze-out near 120 MeV and chemical freeze-out near 140 MeV in central Pb+Pb.

unique_capabilities.quote: NA44 was the only relativistic heavy-ion experiment to have both deuteron and anti-deuteron results in both p-Pb and Pb-Pb collisions
unique_capabilities.value: Only relativistic heavy-ion experiment with both deuteron and anti-deuteron results in both p-Pb and Pb-Pb collisions (per the 2026 SPS review)
